title: Battlestar Galactica - Bilgepumps Trailer
description:
Battlestar Galactica Deadlock – the thought provoker?
- The Bilgepumps Crew do Navy Con 2020 Online

The Bilge Pumps is probably best described as a laid-back meandering chat on modern naval matters with a historical perspective. It strives to unravel the context and complex detail behind headline events through interviews with those in the know, and wild speculation from those who don't!

In this circumstance therefore we are proud to admit that we’re the ever so slightly zany weekly podcast brought to you by the wonderful people of CIMSEC, and three drips who should know better than to spout ship! The motto of which could be Context, Context, Context… but actually is "China, like all sugary sweets, is only allowed in strict moderation" 

This time though the drips are taking their passions of science fiction, naval history and current affairs… and using it all to take a voyage into the future… come along and see if it unravels along the way!

So here it is using the medium of Battlestar Galactica Deadlock and the Battlestar universe the Bilgepumps crew explore, AI, Robot Boarding Parties, Digital vs Analogue, Flak, EMP & Lasers. 

New & Improved Trailer: https://youtu.be/1cdKEpNoOSo

Original Trailer : https://youtu.be/-7NvreHK2OU  

Part 1/2: AI, Robot Boarding Parties & the delicacy of digital https://youtu.be/nvkGpKtqTQs

Part 2/2: Flak, EMP & Lasers https://youtu.be/gDL_l8ROBIE

For the Regular Bilgepumps Podcast Series: https://the-bilgepumps.simplecast.com/

Your Bilgepumps Crew

1.      Dr. Alex Clarke's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCE2x...)
Dr Alexander Clarke, Runs the naval history channel of that name which has proved a boon for multiplying the fun of History... Had his interest in naval history ignited at an early age mostly thanks to his grandfather's stories of his great uncles in WWII.
Has since gone the full academic route including a PhD in War Studies from KCL where he studied under Prof Andrew Lambert as part of the Laughton Unit. Before getting into YouTube, he mainly was active on twitter and publishing articles for Global Maritime History where he's also the Ship Research Editor.
Alongside all this, has the joy of being involved in Bilgepumps and the continuing journey that is a YouTube channel, he has a book coming out early next year titled "Tribals, Battles & Darings, the Genesis of the Modern Destroyer".

2.      Drachinifel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/Drachinifel)
Runs the naval history channel of the same name on YouTube, became fascinated with naval history at age 4 on a visit to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard upon seeing HMS Victory. Later trained as an engineer and decided to bring naval history to a wider audience in 2017, leading to many useful collaborations, including this one!

3.      Jamie Seidel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx5-...)
Jamie Seidel (Jamie pronounced as in Outlander and Jamie Lee Curtis, Seidel as "Sigh-dell".) An Australian freelance journalist who gets irritated when finding holes in stories, which is why he obsesses over forgotten fleets and ignored carrier battles.

For the Regular Bilgepumps Podcast Series: https://the-bilgepumps.simplecast.com/


Your Bilgepumps Crew

1.      Dr. Alex Clarke's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCE2x09tU0GwAGiSbFPEhIwQ/)
Dr Alexander Clarke, Runs the naval history channel of that name which has proved a boon for multiplying the fun of History... Had his interest in naval history ignited at an early age mostly thanks to his grandfather's stories of his great uncles in WWII.
Has since gone the full academic route including a PhD in War Studies from KCL where he studied under Prof Andrew Lambert as part of the Laughton Unit. Before getting into YouTube, he mainly was active on twitter and publishing articles for Global Maritime History where he's also the Ship Research Editor.
Alongside all this, has the joy of being involved in Bilgepumps and the continuing journey that is a YouTube channel, he has a book coming out early next year titled "Tribals, Battles & Darings, the Genesis of the Modern Destroyer".

2.      Drachinifel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/Drachinifel)
Runs the naval history channel of the same name on YouTube, became fascinated with naval history at age 4 on a visit to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard upon seeing HMS Victory. Later trained as an engineer and decided to bring naval history to a wider audience in 2017, leading to many useful collaborations, including this one!

3.      Jamie Seidel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx5-bVhJD0qTT0_A-zXKo0A)
Jamie Seidel (Jamie pronounced as in Outlander and Jamie Lee Curtis, Seidel as "Sigh-dell".) An Australian freelance journalist who gets irritated when finding holes in stories, which is why he obsesses over forgotten fleets and ignored carrier battles.

title: What if Germany didn't invade Belgium in 1914?
description:
A thought experiment started by Patreon 70 

00:00 What if Germany didn't invade Belgium in 1914?
12:00 Part 2
24:00 Part 3
36:00 Part 4
48:00 Part 5
01:00:00 Part 6
01:12:00 End 

For those interested in terms of potential French naval involvement, there is a pretty good overview of their dispositions here https://www.naval-history.net/WW1NavyFrench.htm

And for those interested in one of the many books which have shaped my opinion that the Anglo-American relationship by about 1910 has reached the point of technological rivalry, not getting in the way when the other makes a mistake/active diplomacy to try to imrove their own position, but unlikely to actually go to war with each other - well meet the pilgrim's society https://amzn.to/3XtuRWQ

Now the Prussian/Germans were big fans of War Gaming(https://paxsims.files.wordpress.com/2018/07/wargaming-its-history-and-future.pdf) so this scenario might seem jarring from that perspective. But also remember that Kaiser Wilhelm had taken the absolutely atrocious British government diplomatic signalling to mean acceptance of what was to come... That's one of the reasons he accedes to Moltkes desire to implement the Schlieffen plan, rather than just attack Russia... Similar signalling could well have led them to believe it would be ok.

Finally, please note, I am not making the case for this plan instead of the invasion of Belgium as honestly the issues with this option show exactly strategic & tactical reasons for going through Belgium...

title: Bru Ships Episode 15: Diplomacy & When it Fails, Themed Books to Review & a general Q/A
description:
The Bru Ships series, your sunday afternoon (UK Time) naval history broadly concieved book review and q/a sessions

a very interesting twitter thread on British Embassies https://twitter.com/DefenceDailyUK/status/1294962152458125312?s=19

1) Britain as a Military Power 1688-1815 by Jeremy Black
2) The making of a Civil Servant by Lady Murray (a must read for those interested in RN 1917-36)
3) ReOrient - Global Economy in the Asian Age by Andre Gunder Frank
4) The Battle of the River Plate by Dudley Pope

Some More about Sloops

Sloops are the Royal Navy's answer to Article 8 of the 1930 London Naval Treaty - download a copy from congress here: https://books.googleusercontent.com/books/content?req=AKW5Qafme_NqjB45kczUmWCiyXL_PVHYkeUfEvOjWe1lAcL0kCBRG4vOCPh1RNZBv4R2weaHfr9ceHC1ROBeSk5LIgESQDoOvFZMXtvI7tfIV3mBCQuRA0GHPzxQPc_P3yXwX-42qa_BC814yYsGYQ24_mUudgUuBuKXfUESR5m-U5KmB7Fu_upE1_vJdJZt2TkpCmpkrJtA-VnxvAK3PIwHcijHG3lT2ZnvMRias8tO6a1H3NwzsFy0Sa1RybsfXGwDgiBY8jiAkWcuBkEGdjfwTSzDYGaQ7A
-----
ARTICLE 8.
Subject to any special agreements which may submit them to limitation , the following vessels are exempt from limitation:
(a) naval surface combatant vessels of 600 tons (610 metric tons) standard displacement and under;
(b) naval surface combatant vessels exceeding 600 tons (610 metric tons), but not exceeding 2,000 tons (2,032 metric tons) standard displacement, provided they have none of the following characteristics:
(1) mount a gun above 6.1- inch ( 155 mm. ) calibre;
(2) mount more than four guns above 3 -inch (76 mm .) calibre;
(3) are designed or fitted to launch torpedoes;
(4) are designed for a speed greater than twenty knots.
(c) naval surface vessels not specifically built as fighting ships which are employed on fleet duties or 'as troop transports or in some other way than as fighting ships, provided they have none of the following characteristics:
(1) mount a gun above 6.1 - inch ( 155 mm .) calibre ;
(2) mount more than four guns above 3 -inch (76 mm. ) calibre ;
(3) are designed or fitted to launch torpedoes ;
(4) are designed for a speed greater than twenty knots;
(5) are protected by armourplate; 
(6) are designed or fitted to launch mines;
(7) are fitted to receive aircraft on board from the air;
(8) mount more than one aircraft- launching apparatus on the centre line ; or two, one on each broadside;
(9) if fitted with any means of launching aircraft into the air, are designed or adapted tooperate at sea more than three aircraft.
----

title: Naval History Writing Competition 2023/2024
description:
So What’s the Question? 

Taking any ship or class cancelled around the time of the Washington treaty, develop a logical line of reasoning for it not to be cancelled, then discuss how it affects the 1920s & 30s, how that impacts the subsequent treaties, whether it’s refitted and how it affects WWII

Prize/Results 

The Top Ten will get discussed in a video, with sections read out – but won’t be published in full to leave the option open to the writers to do so at their discretion
Two entrants will receive copies of Tribals, Battles & Darings (paperback)
The one which the judges consider the best
The one which grabs our hearts the most… 

Criteria/Advice  

It has to be over 3,000 but not more than 10,001 words in length
It has to span from end of WWI to at some point in WWII(end point is up to author)
It can be any ship which is cancelled or not built because of or for the Washington Treaty… 
You can even go down potential routes such as unbuilt Admiral Class battlecruisers being used for aircraft carriers or routes not travelled such as the F3 class design 
However, the ships can’t be a secret(it just would not be possible to build a whole ship in secret) and if you are making changes to treaties for these ships you have to discuss how they would affect other powers. But that does not mean you have to give a full history of those changes, it’s just important to acknowledge it to show your thinking 

Process 

All will be submitted to this email address competition@acnavalhistory.com (which has kindly been set up by GariusTheBrit!) prior to the 27th of March 2024, 12:00hrs GMT 
Alex(Dr Clarke) will read through all of them
The final ten will go to the enhanced ship shape team
Drachinifel
GariusTheBrit
Dr Dan
Glynn Stewart
If there is a tie to be decided it will be by Alex

09:00 ​if the Italians had taken Cubinerti seriously, or the US had laid down South Carolina in 1905, how would that have impacted the HMS Dreadnought development?

title: The Force K Long Patrol; Economic Warfare Royal Navy Style
description:
The long Patrol Examining Force K it's service and legacy within the Royal Navy

Force K begins WWII as the name of a critical heavy hitting anti-surface raider force... but by 1941, and re-introduced in 1942 it was name of a critical surface raiding force… It’s differing composition reflected it’s differing role and the geostrategic scenario it was operating under, but also serves as a further reminder that the RN did surface raiding – in fact they were arguably the most successful navy to have ever prosecuted economic/logistically focused warfare such as this…

title: Bilgepumps does Battlestar Galatica Deadlock for Navy Con 2/2
description:
Battlestar Galactica Deadlock – the thought provoker?
- The Bilgepumps Crew do Navy Con 2020 Online

The Bilge Pumps is probably best described as a laid-back meandering chat on modern naval matters with a historical perspective. It strives to unravel the context and complex detail behind headline events through interviews with those in the know, and wild speculation from those who don't!

In this circumstance therefore we are proud to admit that we’re the ever so slightly zany weekly podcast brought to you by the wonderful people of CIMSEC, and three drips who should know better than to spout ship! The motto of which could be Context, Context, Context… but actually is "China, like all sugary sweets, is only allowed in strict moderation" 

This time though the drips are taking their passions of science fiction, naval history and current affairs… and using it all to take a voyage into the future… come along and see if it unravels along the way!

So here it is using the medium of Battlestar Galactica Deadlock and the Battlestar universe the Bilgepumps crew explore, AI, Robot Boarding Parties, Digital vs Analogue, Flak, EMP & Lasers. 

New & Improved Trailer: https://youtu.be/1cdKEpNoOSo

Original Trailer : https://youtu.be/-7NvreHK2OU  

Part 1/2: AI, Robot Boarding Parties & the delicacy of digital https://youtu.be/nvkGpKtqTQs

Part 2/2: Flak, EMP & Lasers https://youtu.be/gDL_l8ROBIE

For the Regular Bilgepumps Podcast Series: https://the-bilgepumps.simplecast.com/


Your Bilgepumps Crew

1.      Dr. Alex Clarke's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCE2x09tU0GwAGiSbFPEhIwQ/)
Dr Alexander Clarke, Runs the naval history channel of that name which has proved a boon for multiplying the fun of History... Had his interest in naval history ignited at an early age mostly thanks to his grandfather's stories of his great uncles in WWII.
Has since gone the full academic route including a PhD in War Studies from KCL where he studied under Prof Andrew Lambert as part of the Laughton Unit. Before getting into YouTube, he mainly was active on twitter and publishing articles for Global Maritime History where he's also the Ship Research Editor.
Alongside all this, has the joy of being involved in Bilgepumps and the continuing journey that is a YouTube channel, he has a book coming out early next year titled "Tribals, Battles & Darings, the Genesis of the Modern Destroyer".

2.      Drachinifel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/Drachinifel)
Runs the naval history channel of the same name on YouTube, became fascinated with naval history at age 4 on a visit to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard upon seeing HMS Victory. Later trained as an engineer and decided to bring naval history to a wider audience in 2017, leading to many useful collaborations, including this one!

3.      Jamie Seidel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx5-bVhJD0qTT0_A-zXKo0A)
Jamie Seidel (Jamie pronounced as in Outlander and Jamie Lee Curtis, Seidel as "Sigh-dell".) An Australian freelance journalist who gets irritated when finding holes in stories, which is why he obsesses over forgotten fleets and ignored carrier battles.

title: SS Streonhalh; the Last Victim of the Admiral Graf Spee - A River Plate 80 Video
description: So this video is the story of the Admiral Graf Spee last victim, the SS Streonhalh - plus has a small issue of me saying Henderson rather than Harwood, which I could have recorded over... but I think sometimes it is important to show that we all make mistakes, I know when I started out in History, as a Dyslexic I was conscious of all the efforts to be perfect, I worried I would never be able to match... now I know its more important to try your best to do justice to the History.

The Quick Summary of the Strengths... The Japanese were... 
- Outnumbered 5:3 in carriers
- Outnumbered 7:5 in battleships
- Their superiority of 3 heavy cruisers could not out vote the 11 light cruisers and 37 destroyers on the American side of the scale… 
- Outnumbered 7:6 in submarines 
- 900 carrier aircraft to 450 carrier & 350 land based aircraft… 
Yet still they sought the decisive battle that had been the cornerstone of their strategy since the Battle of Tsushima.

title: 50th Proper Live Stream - Bru Ships Episode 10: Naval Warfare Themed Books to Review & a general Q/A
description:
The Bru Ships series, your sunday afternoon (UK Time) naval history broadly concieved book review and q/a sessions - as long as the Bru lasts, the questions will be answered.

So yes this will be a bit of a party, this is my 50th Live Episode... i.e. not one that is a test or a random proof of concept, but an actual planned, prepared for episode... I'm not sure I thought about it reaching this point when I started these roughly 15 weeks ago... thank you to all my subscribers, my viewers and to veryone who chats... You have made lockdown flyby and given me something which is going to provide many joyous hours of occupation as my life goes on.

title: Bilge Pumps does Battlestar Galactica Deadlock for Navy Con 1/2
description:
Battlestar Galactica Deadlock – the thought provoker?
- The Bilgepumps Crew do Navy Con 2020 Online

The Bilge Pumps is probably best described as a laid-back meandering chat on modern naval matters with a historical perspective. It strives to unravel the context and complex detail behind headline events through interviews with those in the know, and wild speculation from those who don't!

In this circumstance therefore we are proud to admit that we’re the ever so slightly zany weekly podcast brought to you by the wonderful people of CIMSEC, and three drips who should know better than to spout ship! The motto of which could be Context, Context, Context… but actually is "China, like all sugary sweets, is only allowed in strict moderation" 

This time though the drips are taking their passions of science fiction, naval history and current affairs… and using it all to take a voyage into the future… come along and see if it unravels along the way!

So here it is using the medium of Battlestar Galactica Deadlock and the Battlestar universe the Bilgepumps crew explore, AI, Robot Boarding Parties, Digital vs Analogue, Flak, EMP & Lasers. 

New & Improved Trailer: https://youtu.be/1cdKEpNoOSo

Original Trailer : https://youtu.be/-7NvreHK2OU  

Part 1/2: AI, Robot Boarding Parties & the delicacy of digital https://youtu.be/nvkGpKtqTQs

Part 2/2: Flak, EMP & Lasers https://youtu.be/gDL_l8ROBIE

For the Regular Bilgepumps Podcast Series: https://the-bilgepumps.simplecast.com/


Your Bilgepumps Crew

1.      Dr. Alex Clarke's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCE2x09tU0GwAGiSbFPEhIwQ/)
Dr Alexander Clarke, Runs the naval history channel of that name which has proved a boon for multiplying the fun of History... Had his interest in naval history ignited at an early age mostly thanks to his grandfather's stories of his great uncles in WWII.
Has since gone the full academic route including a PhD in War Studies from KCL where he studied under Prof Andrew Lambert as part of the Laughton Unit. Before getting into YouTube, he mainly was active on twitter and publishing articles for Global Maritime History where he's also the Ship Research Editor.
Alongside all this, has the joy of being involved in Bilgepumps and the continuing journey that is a YouTube channel, he has a book coming out early next year titled "Tribals, Battles & Darings, the Genesis of the Modern Destroyer".

2.      Drachinifel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/Drachinifel)
Runs the naval history channel of the same name on YouTube, became fascinated with naval history at age 4 on a visit to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard upon seeing HMS Victory. Later trained as an engineer and decided to bring naval history to a wider audience in 2017, leading to many useful collaborations, including this one!

3.      Jamie Seidel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx5-bVhJD0qTT0_A-zXKo0A)
Jamie Seidel (Jamie pronounced as in Outlander and Jamie Lee Curtis, Seidel as "Sigh-dell".) An Australian freelance journalist who gets irritated when finding holes in stories, which is why he obsesses over forgotten fleets and ignored carrier battles.

title: What if Washington allowed more than Nelson & Rodney: A UAD infused discussion (Long Patrol)
description:
Please note images and videos are used within this live with the very kind and prompt permission from the Ultimate Admiral: Dreadnoughts game https://www.dreadnoughts.ultimateadmiral.com/ lovely people to liase with and very, very helpful, couldn't have nicer people to chat with.

Thanks to the Tiger UAD infused videos & the Sisters videos I got the idea of what would a Nelson/Rodney equivalent look like (potentially) if the RN had been allowed to sacrifice all the 13.5in gun ships for 16in gun vessels.
That is instead of just Ajax, Thunderer, Cenutrion and King George V, but also Benbow, Emperor of India, Iron Duke, Marlborough and even Tiger... this could be enough to allow a class of 5 (if the limit is 525,000tons) or even 6(if the higher agreed limit of 558,950tons that allowed both Nelson & Rodney is still used) vessels. Would they still go for NelRod design or would they go for an F3 style fast battleship of 28kts? Well this video is a starting point for that discussion.

title: USS Wichita: Comment Response
description:
Furthermore Paul From Chicago went off got the research done to back up his list (including quoting an article written by me), what follows is an excerpt of his last response:

Almost all Town Class had ASDIC:
Friedman's British Cruisers shows ASDIC on the Southhampton. "Note the DF loop on her foremast and the Asdic dome (a feature of many British cruisers) under her bow." Southhampton was the lead ship of the Town Class and it seems likely this was extended to the other Towns, particularly with ASDIC on so many other Towns.
HMS Edinbourgh had ASDIC: https://globalmaritimehistory.com/royal-navy-cruisers-3-hms-edinburgh-a-golden-life/
Sheffield had ASDIC: https://uboat.net/allies/warships/ship/1232.html
Belfast has ASDIC, she's sitting on the Thames so go look. Also, Briane Lavery's The Last Big Gun: At War & At Sea with HMS Belfast and many, many others.

All Crown Colonies had ASDIC:
https://naval-encyclopedia.com/ww2/uk/fiji-class-cruisers.php

It seems likely many Counties had ASDIC as well, as Friedman describes them as fitted for but not with.
HMS Suffolk was refitted with ASDIC:
https://uboat.net/allies/warships/ship/1181.html
Shropshire had ASDIC as well. (Friedman)
Berwick had ASDIC (SIC)

Adventure had ASDIC (SIC). So did the Didos, Arethusas, and Leanders.

I demonstrated above the Hippers had sonar.

The French struggled with sonar, but designed cruisers with sonar in mind. Moulan and Jordan's French Cruisers, 1922–1956 (there's an entire section on underwater sensors).

The Japanese liked sonar on their cruisers and put hydrophones on them. A simple search of Wikipedia will turn up several examples like Agara and Nagano.
Pre-war the Japanese were putting hydrophones on their battlecruisers. http://www.combinedfleet.com/Mutsu.htm
During the war, the Japanese were putting hydrophones on their battlecruisers. http://www.combinedfleet.com/haruna.htm

Your Bilgepumps Crew

1.      Dr. Alex Clarke's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCE2x09tU0GwAGiSbFPEhIwQ/)
Dr Alexander Clarke, Runs the naval history channel of that name which has proved a boon for multiplying the fun of History... Had his interest in naval history ignited at an early age mostly thanks to his grandfather's stories of his great uncles in WWII.
Has since gone the full academic route including a PhD in War Studies from KCL where he studied under Prof Andrew Lambert as part of the Laughton Unit. Before getting into YouTube, he mainly was active on twitter and publishing articles for Global Maritime History where he's also the Ship Research Editor.
Alongside all this, has the joy of being involved in Bilgepumps and the continuing journey that is a YouTube channel, he has a book coming out early next year titled "Tribals, Battles & Darings, the Genesis of the Modern Destroyer".

2.      Drachinifel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/Drachinifel)
Runs the naval history channel of the same name on YouTube, became fascinated with naval history at age 4 on a visit to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard upon seeing HMS Victory. Later trained as an engineer and decided to bring naval history to a wider audience in 2017, leading to many useful collaborations, including this one!

3.      Jamie Seidel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx5-bVhJD0qTT0_A-zXKo0A)
Jamie Seidel (Jamie pronounced as in Outlander and Jamie Lee Curtis, Seidel as "Sigh-dell".) An Australian freelance journalist who gets irritated when finding holes in stories, which is why he obsesses over forgotten fleets and ignored carrier battles.

title: Task Force Doctrine; How it evolved from WWI to WWII in the big three navys - IJN, RN & USN(Patreon)
description:
Patreon - Claire Clarke: The develoopment of task force doctrine in the RN, USN, and IJN from WWI through the beginning of WWII?

Notes:
- Royal Navy
An interesting article on British & Japanese development from a student of Waseda University https://share.google/MUySgSZzQjHJwxCfc ... 
J Levy’s Royal Navy Fleet Tactics is a good journal article https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0968344512440655 ... 
A pretty interesting read by Corbin Williamson https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/culture-of-military-organizations/royal-navy-19001945/44617BB25827D84FF4766CD51A282C78 

- US Navy
International Journal of Naval History – From Fleet Exercises to Fast Carrier Task Force: The Development of Multicarrier Formations https://ijnh.seahistory.org/from-fleet-exercise-to-fast-carrier-task-force-the-development-of-multicarrier-formations/  
... along with something from the USNI Blog https://blog.usni.org/posts/2022/01/25/the-wrong-conclusions-repeating-the-errors-of-naval-interwar-strategic-thinking 

- Imperial Japanese Navy
If you want some fun on this one… may I recommend a disclosed NSA Document https://www.nsa.gov/portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/cryptologic-quarterly/the_period_between_wars.pdf … 
this article from the Naval War College Review on Midway is also good https://digital-commons.usnwc.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2464&context=nwc-review ... 
Also, a really cool Doctoral Thesis on the subject, from Hong Kong Baptist University https://scholars.hkbu.edu.hk/ws/portalfiles/portal/61522109/G22THFL-034126T.pdf ... 
And the bonus is the Italian impact on the Japanese doctrine https://www.swwresearch.com/post/the-italian-navy-and-japan-strategy-and-hopes-1937-1942 

- Catapults
https://navalmarinearchive.com/research/docs/steam_catapults.html

title: The Leander Class Long Patrol - The Interwar 2nd Class Protected Cruiser?
description:
They Leander Class were generation one of the RN's Inter-War cruiser reset; as a result the other classes that came after them are products of them… Whether directly in the form of the Amphion class or indirectly in the form of the Town & Arethusa Classes. Due to the fact that the Leander’s weren’t big enough to do what the Towns were needed for, but not small enough to allow the numbers the Arethusa’s would they were the middle option. The Leanders were the middle of the road option, despite coming first and as such spent of their service filling in the gaps – a role they did well.

Your Bilgepumps Crew

1.      Dr. Alex Clarke's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCE2x09tU0GwAGiSbFPEhIwQ/)
Dr Alexander Clarke, Runs the naval history channel of that name which has proved a boon for multiplying the fun of History... Had his interest in naval history ignited at an early age mostly thanks to his grandfather's stories of his great uncles in WWII.
Has since gone the full academic route including a PhD in War Studies from KCL where he studied under Prof Andrew Lambert as part of the Laughton Unit. Before getting into YouTube, he mainly was active on twitter and publishing articles for Global Maritime History where he's also the Ship Research Editor.
Alongside all this, has the joy of being involved in Bilgepumps and the continuing journey that is a YouTube channel, he has a book coming out early next year titled "Tribals, Battles & Darings, the Genesis of the Modern Destroyer".

2.      Drachinifel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/Drachinifel)
Runs the naval history channel of the same name on YouTube, became fascinated with naval history at age 4 on a visit to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard upon seeing HMS Victory. Later trained as an engineer and decided to bring naval history to a wider audience in 2017, leading to many useful collaborations, including this one!

3.      Jamie Seidel's Youtube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx5-bVhJD0qTT0_A-zXKo0A)
Jamie Seidel (Jamie pronounced as in Outlander and Jamie Lee Curtis, Seidel as "Sigh-dell".) An Australian freelance journalist who gets irritated when finding holes in stories, which is why he obsesses over forgotten fleets and ignored carrier battles.

description:
Operation Dynamo: Dunkirk
26th of May – 4th of June
338,226 Soldiers evacuated (60.6%)

Operation Cycle: Le Havre & St Valery-en-Caux
10th – 13th of June
13,196 British & 1,184 French soldiers (2.6%)

Operation Aerial: The French Atlantic Coast, including Cherbourg, Saint-Malo, Brest, Saint-Nazaire, La Pallice, Le Verdon, Bourdeaux, Bayonne & Saint-Jean-de-Luz
15th – 25th of June officially; unofficially to 14th of August by Mediterranean ports
144,171 British, 24,352 Polish, 18,246 French, 4,938 Czech, 163 Belgian – for a total of 191,870 troops (34.4%) along with 30-40,000 civilians. 

Another roughly 13,393 troops (2.4%) troops made it out by other means, either by aircraft, by Spain to Gibraltar or Portugal…

title: The Battle of the Philippine Sea: Live
description:
The Quick Summary of the Strengths... The Japanese were... 
- Outnumbered 5:3 in carriers
- Outnumbered 7:5 in battleships
- Their superiority of 3 heavy cruisers could not out vote the 11 light cruisers and 37 destroyers on the American side of the scale… 
- Outnumbered 7:6 in submarines 
- 900 carrier aircraft to 450 carrier & 350 land based aircraft… 
Yet still they sought the decisive battle that had been the cornerstone of their strategy since the Battle of Tsushima.
